legend: You have 2n$$$2n$$$ integers 1,2,…,2n$$$1, 2, \dots, 2n$$$. You have to redistribute these 2n$$$2n$$$ elements into n$$$n$$$ pairs. After that, you choose x$$$x$$$ pairs and take minimum elements from them, and from the other n−x$$$n - x$$$ pairs, you take maximum elements.
Your goal is to obtain the set of numbers {b1,b2,…,bn}$$$\{b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n\}$$$ as the result of taking elements from the pairs.

What is the number of different x$$$x$$$-s (0≤x≤n$$$0 \le x \le n$$$) such that it's possible to obtain the set b$$$b$$$ if for each x$$$x$$$ you can choose how to distribute numbers into pairs and from which x$$$x$$$ pairs choose minimum elements?
input: The first line contains a single integer t$$$t$$$ (1≤t≤1000$$$1 \le t \le 1000$$$) — the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case contains the integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤2⋅105$$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$).
The second line of each test case contains n$$$n$$$ integers b1,b2,…,bn$$$b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$$$ (1≤b1<b2<⋯<bn≤2n$$$1 \le b_1  \lt  b_2  \lt  \dots  \lt  b_n \le 2n$$$) — the set you'd like to get.

output: For each test case, print one number — the number of different x$$$x$$$-s such that it's possible to obtain the set b$$$b$$$.
note: In the first test case, x=1$$$x = 1$$$ is the only option: you have one pair (1,2)$$$(1, 2)$$$ and choose the minimum from this pair.

In the second test case, there are three possible x$$$x$$$-s. You can take minimum from (1,6)$$$(1, 6)$$$ (equal to 1$$$1$$$) and the maximum elements from all other pairs to get set b$$$b$$$.
In the third test case, x=0$$$x = 0$$$ is the only option: you can form pairs (1,3)$$$(1, 3)$$$, (2,4)$$$(2, 4)$$$ and take the maximum elements from both of them.
